title: No Steering Wheel? No Problem! Zoox's Robot Taxis Can Now Charge You for a Ride
summary: Have you ever dreamed of a car that drives itself, like in a sci-fi movie? Well, that dream just got a little more real. Zoox, a company owned by Amazon, just got special permission to charge people for rides in its robotaxis. And here's the coolest part: these cars don't have steering wheels or pedals! They're built from the ground up to be driven by computers, not humans. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) gave Zoox the thumbs-up on Thursday. It's the first time ever that a car without traditional controls can pick up paying passengers in the U.S. Zoox has been giving free rides in Las Vegas since last year, and now it can finally start earning money. It's also testing in Austin, Miami, and San Francisco—all for free, for now. So, what's it like inside? The seats face each other, like you're sitting around a campfire. You can chat with your friends or just enjoy the ride. No driver's seat, no dashboard—just space to hang out. Waymo, another big robotaxi company, still uses cars with steering wheels and pedals, even if no one touches them. Zoox thinks that to make driverless tech really shine, cars need to be designed differently. But it wasn't easy. Zoox worked for over ten years to design, build, and get government approval for these weird and wonderful vehicles. The NHTSA's approval is a two-year exemption from normal safety rules. Zoox can put up to 5,000 robotaxis on the road, but it has to share extra data on crashes and weird stops. If something seems unsafe, the government can take back the permission. NHTSA boss Jonathan Morrison said Zoox proved its cars are even safer than regular ones. He also warned that if there's any danger, "you're going to hear from us." Earlier this month, he wrote a letter about robotaxis getting in the way of firefighters and police. Zoox says it has already given over 500,000 rides and driven more than 3 million miles without a human driver. That's a lot of practice! But the company only has about 105 active robotaxis right now, so getting to 5,000 will take a while. Still, this is a huge step. Next time you're in Vegas, you might just hop into a car with no steering wheel and let the future drive you home.
why_it_matters: One day you might ride to school or a friend's house in a car that steers itself—like a magic carriage with no driver.
